claims.text: Typed money is compared as whole cents, so 2810.5 and $2,810.50 are the same amount and 12.3 is not 12.34.
Typed words match the sheet even with extra spaces or different capital letters.
A different answer is named in plain words, with what was typed and what the sheet says.
An answer that was not typed yet is named, and the sheet value is shown.
The summary says all answers match only when every answer matches.
The practice sheet holds made-up answers only: no Social Security number, no bank number, and only example.com emails.
The page has no Submit button and no form that submits. It tells the person to press Submit on the real IRS partner site.
Messy typing never throws and never gives NaN, and a bad sheet gets a plain-words problem.
